concepts.why: The patient's history of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and the presence of a cluster of small-bowel loops in the left upper quadrant, positioned anterior to the splenic flexure, suggest internal hernia as a possible diagnosis.
The patient's symptoms of abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting, as well as the presence of generalized abdominal tenderness, suggest adhesive bowel obstruction as a possible diagnosis.
The patient's symptoms of abdominal pain and the presence of normal laboratory tests, including lactate level, suggest intestinal ischemia as a possible diagnosis.
The patient's history of multiple surgeries, including Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, and the presence of intermittent nausea, suggest post-surgical adhesions as a possible diagnosis.

The patient's symptoms of abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting, as well as the presence of a cluster of small-bowel loops in the left upper quadrant, suggest small bowel obstruction as a possible diagnosis.
The patient's symptoms of abdominal pain and the presence of generalized abdominal tenderness, suggest intra-abdominal abscess as a possible diagnosis.
The patient's history of multiple surgeries, including Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, and the presence of intermittent nausea, suggest gastrointestinal fistula as a possible diagnosis.
The patient's symptoms of abdominal pain and the presence of normal laboratory tests, including lactate level, suggest mesenteric venous thrombosis as a possible diagnosis.
The patient's history of type 2 diabetes mellitus managed with pantoprazole, metformin, and semaglutide explains the nausea and vomiting, which are symptoms of diabetic gastroparesis.
